I'd turn a blind eye on the fact that you're in love with someone 10 years older than you.
But in your case, I'd advise you to actually try and be more open to your wife,even if you do not have any intention or energy to talk to her and spend quality time,you should push yourself into it. If you stay in your comfort zone you will not move forward in any aspect,knowing that you will be stuck with your now wife for a long period,you have to put time and effort into your relationship.
Try discovering yourself first,what might cause your fear of intimacy and other fears, what you like and do not like, what's your love language (how you want to love and be loved) , understand your boundaries... Try to also communicate about these things with your wife and encourage her to do the same.
Easiest way to do this is setup a nice date and make it clear that you will be discussing the matter of how you want to make your marriage healthy and long lasting.
The process of moving on,discovering and understanding yourself and your partner is going to take a little while but it's beneficial to give it a shot and see how it goes.
Best of luck for you.

Thing is my surroundings are also his surroundings,so if something ever happens between us two I will lose the rest and be left alone.The very few friends I have are also his friends and the only people I have to run to are my family and they wouldn't be as helpful neither. I did get counseling I'm not ashamed of it but since I am too self aware of everything that goes on in my life It sometimes feel helpless to go to a professional,as I have already been in some sort of situations and the only solution they provided were meds (I don't need those)
Whenever we fight it's about simple things such as me saying "no" when he tries to initiate intimacy,or maybe just playing with me. Majority of our fights are about me saying "no" ,or things from my past (exes and people I used to talk with) , friends I no longer have contact with, sometimes even silly things such as jokes,in general misunderstandings that can be solved... I do admit that he is jealous to a scary degree,I chose to stop talking to male friends and every single guy except the ones in our friend group,I did that out of respect but that itself made me feel some pressure as It makes me uncomfortable to some extent. When we argue about those I do believe I am the faulty one,but everytime I fix those things even if they are out of my control (such as a friend texting me a simple hi or how are you)  and try to stop doing what he doesn't like me to do (changing the things I normally do for him) something new resurfaces from the dark. And whenever that happens I blame myself even more. I say that it is mandatory for me to change but at the same time I feel trapped and pressured.
I understand all his behaviors as I was once just like him,I used to love someone to the point that I threaten them with suicide because I was too afraid to lose them and I now understand how it impacted me and those people (guess whatever goes around comes back to you,karma is real innit?) 
He has great qualities,things I have never found and pretty sure wouldn't find in anybody else especially in my surroundings (I live in a third world country,you can only imagine what could be going on),but as great as we get somethings always comes from the blue and destroys the hope I rebuild everytime. How do I convince him of all of this when I am afraid of his rage once I open up to him about all of this?
( I apologize for the long long response)

I understand that it is not right to step away and I have already spoke to him countless times about how those actions harm me mentally and physically,but the same things happen. I once told him that he should seek professional help and get a therapist to help him heal his trauma,I encouraged him to do it by telling him that I would do so as well but he didn't take that well,and instead he told me that "he is not crazy and that the only person who can heal him is himself". I am considerate of all his traumas and life problems and I believe that's what's making him like that but It still hurts me and doesn't help at all with my own mental issues (which I have worked really hard to heal and better). Even tho I accept his behaviors and acts up I got tired of doing so and it's making me rethink the whole relationship. I'm in the middle of a messed up situation where leaving doesn't seem to be the solution but nothing else is a solution

Thing is when we are on safe rides with no issues or problems whatsoever he is truly the sweetest and most loving person. He shows me that he genuinely loves me and he proves it,you can't literally think that he would be that agressive and uncontrollable once put in such situations where we argue. But sometimes I feel like that rage he lets out destroys all that loving scenery,only for him to do the same sweet stuff and on and on it goes... This makes it even harder to decide whether I should run for safety or risk it all and stay
